explanation: King of Judah who sought God's help against the Assyrians and their king Sennacherib.
King of Assyria who threatened Hezekiah and Jerusalem, and mocked the God of Israel.
The capital city of the kingdom of Judah, the site of Solomon's temple and the center of Jewish faith.
An important prophet in the Old Testament who delivered God's words and promises to Hezekiah.
A communication with God where people express their desires, gratitude, or concerns.
A holy place where people worship and offer sacrifices to God; in this case, it refers to Solomon's temple in Jerusalem.
Spiritual beings created by God to serve him and carry out his will; in this context, an angel destroyed the Assyrian army.
The people from the ancient empire of Assyria, known for their military power and conquests.
